extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent owners, licensees, IP practitioners and national IP office / court officials (Member States to the Bangui Agreement)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural/substantive criteria for granting, amending, transferring, enforcing and appealing non-voluntary (compulsory) patent licenses, counterfeiting enforcement (civil, criminal, border measures) and the definition, protection and formal requirements for utility models under the Annex (Bangui Agreement).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and opportunity to be heard in non-voluntary license proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The court shall notify the owner of the patent and any licensee whose name appears in the register of patents, and shall invite them to submit written observations on the application within three months; such observations shall be communicated to the applicant; the court shall likewise notify the application to any government authorities concerned; the court shall hold a hearing on the application and the observations received, to which the applicant, the owner of the patent, any licensee whose name appears in the register of patents and any government authorities concerned shall be summonsed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes procedural notice, a three-month period for written observations, communication of observations to the applicant, notification to government authorities and a formal hearing with summons to all interested parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court decision on non-voluntary license request
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the prescribed proceedings have been completed, the court shall rule on the request, either granting or refusing the non-voluntary license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Binary judicial determination after hearing and consideration of observations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of grant decision: scope of non-voluntary license
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the non-voluntary license is granted, the decision of the court shall specify the scope of the license, specifying in particular the acts referred to in Article 6(3) of this Annex which it encompasses and the period for which it is granted, it being understood that a non-voluntary license granted under Article 49 or 50 above may not encompass the act of importation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court must expressly define which acts (manufacture, use, sale, etc.), territorial and temporal limits; certain grants (under Articles 49/50) may not include importation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of grant decision: remuneration for licensee
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision of the court shall specify the amount of the remuneration owed by the licensee to the owner of the patent; failing agreement between the parties, such remuneration shall be equitable, with due regard to all the circumstances of the case; the amount of the remuneration shall be subject to judicial review on application by the beneficiary of the non-voluntary license or the patentee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remuneration to be set by agreement or as equitable compensation by court considering all circumstances; either party may seek judicial review of amount.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasoned decision and registration/publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The decision of the court shall be reasoned. Once the decision is final, it shall be transmitted to the Organization by the more diligent party; the Organization shall enter it into the special register and publish a notice thereof; the Organization shall notify the decision to any licensee whose name appears in the special register of patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions must include reasons, be communicated to Organization, registered and published; notification obligations to affected licensees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of grant when final: authorization and payment obligation
rubrics_metrics.description: After the expiry of the time limit for appeal or once an appeal decision upholds the grant, the grant of the license shall authorize the licensee to work the patented invention according to the terms laid down in the decision and shall require him to pay the remuneration specified in the judicial decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finality of decision triggers licensee's right to exploit under specified terms and obligation to pay set remuneration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility of non-voluntary license with other licenses and non-discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: The grant of a non-voluntary license shall not affect either license contracts in force or non-voluntary licenses in force and shall not preclude the conclusion of other license contracts or the grant of other non-voluntary licenses. However, the patentee may not grant to other licensees more favorable terms than those of the non-voluntary license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-voluntary license coexists with existing licenses but patentee cannot give superior terms to others (no undermining the compulsory license's terms).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation on beneficiary granting sublicenses
rubrics_metrics.description: A beneficiary of a non-voluntary license may not grant any third party permission to perform any of the acts that he is authorized to perform under the non-voluntary license without the consent of the owner of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibits sublicensing without patentee consent, protecting patentee control over exploitation by third parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transfer of non-voluntary license with establishment
rubrics_metrics.description: Notwithstanding the prohibition on granting permissions, a non-voluntary license may be transferred together with the establishment of the beneficiary or with the portion of his establishment that exploits the patented invention. No such transfer shall be valid without the authorization of the competent domestic court; before granting the authorization, the court shall afford the owner of the patent a hearing; the court shall notify the authorization to the Organization, which shall register and publish it. Any transfer authorized shall mean that the new beneficiary shall accept the same obligations as those that were incumbent on the former beneficiary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transfers allowed only with court authorization, prior hearing of patentee, registration and continuity of obligations for transferee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of non-voluntary license decision on new facts
rubrics_metrics.description: On the request of the owner of the patent or the beneficiary, the competent domestic court may amend the decision on the grant of the non-voluntary license where new facts justify such amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides mechanism to revisit license terms if material new facts emerge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for withdrawal of non-voluntary license
rubrics_metrics.description: At the request of the owner of the patent, the competent domestic court shall withdraw the non-voluntary license: (a) if the grounds for its grant have ceased to exist; (b) if the beneficiary exceeds the scope of the license; or (c) if the beneficiary is in arrears with the payment of the remuneration. In situations (a) and (b), the withdrawal may be requested by other licensees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies clear grounds on which patentee can seek withdrawal; other licensees may also request withdrawal in certain cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection for beneficiary upon withdrawal for ceased grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the non-voluntary license is withdrawn under the ground that the grounds for its grant have ceased to exist, the beneficiary shall be allowed a reasonable period within which to cease working the invention, where immediate cessation would have serious adverse consequences for him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court must allow reasonable wind-down period to prevent severe hardship on beneficiary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal rights and suspensive effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Within one month of publication, the owner of the patent, the licensee whose name appears in the special register or any person who has sought the grant of a non-voluntary license may appeal to the competent higher court against a decision taken under Articles 52(3), 54(2) or 55. The appeal contesting the grant, authorization to transfer, or amendment/withdrawal shall have suspensive effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One-month appeal period; appeals against grant/transfer/amendment/withdrawal stay the contested measure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cessation of beneficiary obligations upon final invalidation
rubrics_metrics.description: If a final legal judgement declares the patent invalid, the beneficiary of the non-voluntary license shall be released from all obligations resulting from the decision granting him the non-voluntary license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final invalidation of patent extinguishes licensee's obligations under the compulsory license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative non-voluntary licenses in national interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent is vital to the economy, public health or national defense, or where its non-working or insufficient working severely jeopardizes meeting the country's needs, it may be subjected to non-voluntary licensing by administrative order of the competent Minister.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ministerial (administrative) route for compulsory licensing when public interest or insufficient working threatens national needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of administrative order for national-interest license
rubrics_metrics.description: The administrative order shall determine after negotiation the term of the license; the scope of the license, in particular authorized acts including importation, quantities and territorial scope; and the amount of the fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative order must set term, scope (may include importation), quantities and fees; negotiated among interested parties or fixed by minister if no agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ministerial fixation and judicial revision of conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Failing amicable agreement between owner and administration on conditions, the conditions shall be fixed by authority of the competent Minister. However, these conditions may be revised by the competent domestic court seized by the more diligent party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minister can set conditions unilaterally when negotiations fail, but courts can later review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction for patent civil and criminal matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Civil action concerning patents shall be brought before the competent domestic courts and heard as for summary proceedings. Where action for counterfeiting is brought before the competent domestic court for criminal matters, it shall rule on challenges regarding invalidity or forfeiture of the patent, or matters relating to ownership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designates domestic courts for patent litigation and grants criminal courts authority to adjudicate related patent validity/ownership challenges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acts prior to grant not infringement unless notified
rubrics_metrics.description: Acts occurring prior to the grant of a patent shall not be considered to have infringed the rights relating thereto. However, acts may be recorded and prosecuted where they occur after notification to the alleged counterfeiter of an official copy of the specification of the invention attached to the patent application. In such case, the competent domestic court seized shall suspend its ruling until the publication of the grant of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited provisional protection post-notification; courts suspend rulings until grant publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim of ownership and time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a patent is issued or acquired for an invention in infringement of the rights of the inventor or in violation of a legal/contractual obligation, the injured party may claim ownership. Action to establish title shall be brought within three years of the publication of the grant or acquisition. In case of bad faith at time of grant/acquisition, the time limit shall be three years with effect from the exhaustion of the patent right.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides standing and prescription periods for ownership claims; final transfer decisions to be notified and registered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of counterfeiting and proof standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Any infringement of the rights of the patent owner, by making use of the means that are the object of his patent, by concealment, by sale or offering for sale or by bringing into the territory of a Member State, shall constitute counterfeiting. Counterfeiting may be proven by all means.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad definition covering various acts; flexible evidentiary standard (proof by all means).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standing to bring counterfeiting action
rubrics_metrics.description: Action for counterfeiting shall be brought by the patentee. Nonetheless, the beneficiary of an exclusive right of working and the holder of a non-voluntary license may bring action for counterfeiting, unless otherwise provided, if after notice the patentee does not avail himself of this right within three months. Any licensee may intervene in action for counterfeiting to obtain reparation for his own prejudice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patentee primary plaintiff; beneficiaries and licensees have conditional standing/intervention rights to protect their interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim (urgent/ex parte) measures to prevent infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person empowered to bring action may make an urgent application seeking, if necessary under financial compulsion, an order against the alleged counterfeiter or intermediaries instituting any measure intended to prevent an imminent infringement or the continuation of alleged infringement. The court may also order urgent measures ex parte where delay is likely to be irreparably prejudicial, but only if reasonably accessible evidence makes it likely that rights are being infringed or that such infringement is imminent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows urgent and ex parte relief where necessary; requires prima facie evidence; provides safeguards (financial compulsion, evidence threshold).

rubrics_metrics.name: Powers available in urgent measures
rubrics_metrics.description: The court may prohibit continuation of alleged acts, make acts contingent on guarantees intended to secure compensation for the applicant, or order seizure or transfer to a third party of products suspected of infringing to prevent their introduction or circulation in commercial channels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Range of provisional remedies includes prohibition, conditional continuation, seizure/transfer to prevent commercial distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guarantee requirement and risk of cancellation of measures
rubrics_metrics.description: On receipt of an urgent or ex parte application, the court may make measures contingent on provision of guarantees by the applicant to compensate the defendant if proceedings are later found to be without basis or measures are cancelled. Where measures are ordered before action on the merits, the applicant shall bring action within 20 days following implementation of the measures; otherwise, on application by the defendant (who need not state reasons), the measures shall be cancelled, without prejudice to damages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects defendants by allowing guarantees and strict time limits (20 days) to commence substantive proceedings; failure leads to automatic cancellation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seizure procedure and required authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person with locus standi is entitled to take measures anywhere, including at the border, to effect either a detailed inventory with/without samples, or the physical seizure of allegedly counterfeit products or procedures. Seizure is effected by bailiff/public officer/judicial officer including customs, assisted by experts, following an order by the competent domestic court made on application and on presentation of the patent. Customs shall immediately inform the applicant and the importer of execution. Where grounds for seizure exist the order may require a security deposit; the deposit shall be adequate without deterring applicants and shall always be required of foreigners. The person in possession shall be given a copy of the order and, where appropriate, a copy of the document attesting the deposit on pain of invalidity and damages against the executing officers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seizures require court order and presentation of patent, may involve experts, customs involvement, and security deposit rules intended to balance access with non-deterrence; formal delivery of order and deposit documents is vital to validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time limit to institute proceedings after seizure/inventory
rubrics_metrics.description: Should the applicant fail to institute criminal or legal proceedings within 10 days of the seizure or inventory, such seizure or inventory shall ipso jure be void, without prejudice to any damages that may be claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Very short mandatory deadline (10 days) to begin substantive proceedings after seizure; failure nullifies seizure automatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reverse burden of proof in process-for-product cases
rubrics_metrics.description: For civil proceedings, if the subject matter of the patent is a process for making a product, the court may order the defendant to prove that the process used to make an identical product is different from the patented process where (a) the product made by the process is new; or (b) there is a high probability that the identical product was made by means of the process and the owner was unable, despite reasonable efforts, to establish what process was actually used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shifts evidentiary burden to defendant in certain process/product situations, while safeguarding the defendant's manufacturing secrets if contrary evidence is brought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclosure orders to trace origin and distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: The court may, if necessary under financial compulsion and for purposes of determining origin and distribution networks of counterfeit products or processes, order disclosure of all documentation or information held by the defendant or any person in possession of counterfeit products or applying counterfeit processes or providing services used in counterfeiting, provided there is no legitimate impediment. The documents sought may concern names/addresses of producers, manufacturers, distributors, suppliers and others, and quantities produced, sold, delivered, received or ordered, and the prices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Power to compel wide-ranging disclosure to map networks, subject to legitimate impediments (e.g., privilege) and financial considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation of damages for counterfeiting
rubrics_metrics.description: The court shall calculate the amount of the damages, having regard to the adverse financial effects, including loss of earnings, suffered by the prejudiced party, the profit made by the counterfeiter and the moral damages caused to the title owner as a result of the violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Damages assessment must consider both patentee's losses, counterfeiter's profits, and moral (non-pecuniary) harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitation period for counterfeit proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The counterfeit proceedings provided for in this chapter shall be limited to five years with effect from the date of the alleged acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Five-year statute of limitations from the date of alleged infringing acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal penalties for counterfeiting
rubrics_metrics.description: The offense of counterfeiting shall be punishable by imprisonment for one to three years and a fine of 5,000,000 to 30,000,000 CFA francs or one of these penalties alone, without prejudice to civil damages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies criminal sanctions; does not preclude civil remedies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggravating circumstances doubling penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event of recidivism or aggravating circumstances, the above-mentioned penalties shall be doubled. Recidivism occurs where an offender has been convicted of one of the offenses provided for in this Annex within the five previous years. Penalties shall be doubled if the counterfeiter is a person who has worked or been employed in the workshop/establishment of the patentee or if, in association with a worker/employee of the patentee, thereby had knowledge of the processes described in the patent. The worker/employee may be prosecuted as an accomplice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines recidivism and specific workplace-related aggravating facts that increase sanctions and expose accomplices to prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of mitigating circumstances
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of legislation in Member States regarding mitigating circumstances shall apply to offenses provided for in this Annex.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Domestic law on mitigation governs reduction of penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent initiation of criminal proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Criminal proceedings may be brought concurrently by the Public Prosecutor's Office and the prejudiced party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both state and private parties may initiate criminal enforcement in parallel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional penalties: confiscation, destruction and publicity
rubrics_metrics.description: In the event of a conviction, the competent domestic court shall order the confiscation or destruction of objects found to be counterfeit and, where applicable, the confiscation or destruction of implements or tools specially intended for their manufacture. The court may also order measures to publicize the verdict, including posting or publication in newspapers or online public communication services. These measures may be instituted even in the event of an acquittal. The civil court may order withdrawal from trade channels, permanent removal, destruction or confiscation for benefit of the prejudiced party. Such measures shall be ordered at the cost of the counterfeiter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wide remedial toolbox including destruction, confiscation, publicity and market withdrawal; some publicity measures may be ordered even on acquittal; costs shift to counterfeiter on conviction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usurpation offence and penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who, by means of signs, advertisement, marks or stamps improperly avails himself of the status of owner of a patent issued in accordance with this agreement or after expiry of a previous patent shall be punishable by a fine of 1,000,000 to 5,000,000 CFA francs. In the event of recidivism, the fine may be doubled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Penalizes false claims of patent ownership; escalating sanctions for repeat offenders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Customs detention on request and procedural safeguards
rubrics_metrics.description: Customs administration may, on written application by any person supported by proof of his right, detain goods it suspects to be counterfeit when conducting controls. The public prosecutor, the applicant and the importer shall be immediately informed. The detention shall be lifted ipso jure within 10 working days of notification if the applicant fails to provide proof to customs services of interim measures or of his application to the competent court and provision of requisite guarantees. For purposes of taking legal action, the applicant may request communication by customs of names and addresses of sender, importer and intended recipient of detained goods, their quantity, notwithstanding professional secrecy by which customs officials are bound. On expiry of the 10-day limit, where suspension of free movement is not taken by judicial authority or independent administration, the owner/importer/recipient may, on payment of a security deposit, cause the detention order to be suspended.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets notification obligations, strict 10-working-day automatic lift unless applicant proves steps taken and provides guarantees, limited disclosure rights from customs, and possibility to suspend detention by deposit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ex officio customs detention and liability
rubrics_metrics.description: Customs authorities may ex officio decide to detain suspect goods where they have prima facie evidence that the goods are counterfeit and may at any time request the owner to provide information to assist them. The holder of the right, the importer and the exporter shall be immediately informed of the detention. The liability of customs may be incurred in the event of unjustified detention, save where they acted in good faith.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits proactive customs action on prima facie evidence, with immediate notifications and limited liability protection for good faith actions; exposes customs to liability for unjustified detentions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of utility models (subject matter and criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Utility models protected by registration certificates shall be implements of work or objects intended to be utilized or parts thereof, provided they are useful for the work or intended purpose on account of a new configuration, a new arrangement or a new component device and are industrially applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines utility models by practical usefulness due to specific structural/configurational novelty and industrial applicability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded subject matter from utility model protection
rubrics_metrics.description: The following shall not be considered objects of a utility model: (a) discoveries, scientific theories and mathematical methods; (b) esthetic creations; (c) schemes, rules or methods in performing mental acts, for playing games or in doing business, or computer programs; and (d) presentations of information. The provisions do not exclude protection as a utility model except where protection is requested for the above elements considered as such.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enumerates exclusions (similar to patent exclusions), while clarifying only the listed items are excluded if claimed as such.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty requirement for utility models and limited grace exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: An implement or object shall not be considered new if, on the filing date, they have been described in publications or publicly used on territory of a Member State or third-party State for at least six months. The novelty shall not be denied if, during the twelve months preceding that date, the object was disclosed as a result of manifest abuse against the applicant or displayed at an official or officially recognized international exhibition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Novelty bar includes prior publications or public use for six months before filing; limited 12-month grace for abuse or official exhibition disclosures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial applicability for utility models
rubrics_metrics.description: A utility model shall be considered industrially applicable if its object can be made or used in any kind of industry; 'industry' is to be understood in its broadest sense and includes handicrafts, agriculture, fishery and services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad conception of industrial applicability permitting protection for diverse sectors including services and handicrafts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absolute and relative exclusions for registration
rubrics_metrics.description: A utility model may not be registered if it is contrary to public policy or morality, public health, the national economy or national defense; exploitation is not considered contrary merely because prohibited by law/regulation. No utility model may be protected if it has already been the subject of a patent or utility model registration based on a prior application or an application validly claiming an earlier priority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows refusal on public policy/health/economy/defense grounds and bars double protection where prior rights exist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights conferred by the registration certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to conditions and limits, the owner of a certificate of registration shall have the right to prohibit any person from exploiting the utility model by performing acts: manufacturing, offering for sale, selling and utilizing the utility model, and importing and holding it for purposes of offering it for sale, selling it or utilizing it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the negative/exclusive rights conferred (manufacture, offer, sale, use, import, holding for commercial purposes).

rubrics_metrics.name: Term of protection for utility models
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject to Article 35, the term of protection conferred by the certificate of registration shall expire at the end of the tenth year with effect from the filing date of the application for registration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ten-year maximum term measured from filing date (subject to other provisions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to registration certificate: inventor, priority and competing applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: The right to registration shall belong to the inventor; the applicant shall be deemed owner. If several persons created the same invention independently, the right belongs to the person who filed the application whose filing date or validly claimed priority date is earliest, provided application not withdrawn/abandoned/refused. Joint creators are joint owners. The right may be assigned or transferred by succession. If a person not entitled files an application, the entitled person may institute proceedings for transfer of the application or certificate; proceedings for transfer of application are subject to a five-year time limit from publication of the certificate; proceedings against bad faith defendants are not time-barred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes inventor ownership, first-to-file/priority rules, joint ownership, assignment, and time limits for corrective proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint ownership rights and constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise stipulated: (a) Each joint owner may work the invention to his profit provided he makes fair compensation to other joint owners not personally working it or not granting licenses; (b) Each joint owner may bring action for counterfeiting to his sole benefit (must notify other joint owners); (c) Each joint owner may grant a non-exclusive exploitation license to a third party to his benefit, provided he compensates other joint owners and notifies them with an offer to transfer the share at a specific price; others may challenge/grab the share within three months by purchase; exclusive licenses only with agreement of all joint owners or by leave of court; (e) Each joint owner may assign his share at any time; joint owners have right of first refusal for three months; price disputes determined by court; (f) A joint owner may relinquish his share to others by notification, with discharge of obligations on relinquishment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive regime specifying compensation, notification, rights of first refusal, options to acquire shares, constraints on exclusive licensing, and remedies via courts for price disputes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee and commissioned-works invention ownership and remuneration
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the inventor is an employee, in absence of contractual provisions more favorable to the employee: (a) inventions made in performance of employment contract encompassing an inventive task or expressly assigned studies/research shall belong to the employer; the employee shall receive supplementary remuneration fixed by court if not negotiated; (b) where employee not required to engage in inventive activity but makes an invention using company techniques/means/data, employer has right to be granted ownership or enjoyment of all/part of rights, with fair price fixed by court if no agreement, taking into account contributions and commercial utility; (c) all other inventions belong to employee. Employee must immediately inform employer and both must share useful information and refrain from disclosure; any agreement must be in writing under pain of invalidity. If employer expressly waives right, the right belongs to employee. Provisions also apply to employees of State/public bodies. Inventions made in fulfillment of an order belong to the client unless otherwise provided in the contract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allocates ownership depending on employment duties and use of employer resources; requires remuneration to employee in certain cases; imposes notification, confidentiality and written-agreement requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations/exceptions to utility model rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Rights do not encompass: (a) acts relating to objects offered for sale in territory by owner or with his consent; (b) use of objects on board foreign aircraft/land vehicles/ships that temporarily or accidentally enter territory; (c) acts for experimental purposes in scientific/technical research or for educational purposes; and (d) acts by any person who in good faith on the filing date or priority date was in possession of the utility model. The possessor's right may only be assigned with the goodwill/business or the part to which it is attached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies standard exceptions including exhaustion, experimental use, and prior possession defenses and the limited assignability of prior possessor's right.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal requirements for filing an application for registration of a utility model
rubrics_metrics.description: The application shall be filed with the Organization or the Ministry responsible and the application file shall contain: (a) an application addressed to the Director-General; (b) proof of payment of requisite fees; (c) an unstamped, private power of attorney if represented by an agent; and (d) a sealed envelope containing: (i) a specification stating by what configuration, arrangement or mechanism the utility model may be useful to the intended purpose, set out clearly and completely so that a person having ordinary knowledge and skill in the art could carry out the model; (ii) the drawings and photographs necessary or useful for understanding the specification; (iii) a descriptive abstract summarizing the contents of the specification; (iv) the claim or claims defining the scope of protection sought, which shall not exceed the contents of the specification; and (v) sufficient indications regarding the best manner of carrying out the invention known to the inventor on the filing date and, where priority is claimed, the priority date of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comprehensive checklist of required formal documents and substantive sufficiency of specification, claims, drawings and best mode information; claims must be supported by specification; application must include payment and (if applicable) power of attorney.
